en.name: Pickled beets
en.summary: Commercially jarred pickled beets keep about 1 year unopened in the cupboard. Refrigerate after opening, where they keep 1–2 months — the vinegar carries them a long way, but an opened jar is still a refrigerated food.
en.pantry: An unopened jar keeps about 1 year in a cool, dark cupboard, or to the printed date if that is sooner. The acidity of the pickling liquid is what makes beets shelf-stable, together with the heat processing and the seal; beetroot on its own is a low-acid vegetable and would not keep this way. Keep jars out of direct sunlight, which bleaches the colour badly in something this red, and discard without tasting any jar with a domed lid or one that spurts when you open it.
en.fridge: Refrigerate after opening and use within 1–2 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Keep the beets submerged in their liquid — anything standing proud of the brine dries, darkens and is the first place to grow mould — and use a clean fork each time rather than fingers. Home-pickled beets that were not processed for shelf stability are a refrigerator product from the start and should be treated as such, whatever the recipe implied.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for pickled beets, and freezing them is a poor idea in any case. Beetroot is largely water in firm cells, and freezing bursts those cells, so what thaws is soft, weeping and unpleasantly limp — the crispness that pickling preserved is exactly what a freezer destroys. The refrigerated window is generous enough that there is no need.
spoilage: Mould at the surface of the liquid or under the rim of the lid.
Brine gone cloudy, ropy or thickened.
A domed or leaking lid, or a jar that hisses or spurts on opening.
Beets gone soft and mushy, or a yeasty, fermented smell rather than a clean vinegar one.
tips: Keep the beets under their liquid; exposed pieces spoil first.
Use a clean fork every time, never fingers.
Store jars out of the light — sunlight fades the colour fast.
Write the opening date on the lid; one to two months passes quietly.

faq.q: How long do pickled beets keep once opened?
faq.a: 1–2 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept submerged in their liquid. Unopened, about 1 year in the cupboard.
Not while the jar is sealed. After opening, yes — the label says refrigerate, and an opened jar is no longer protected by its seal.
There is no timeline for it and it is not worth doing — freezing bursts the cells and they thaw limp and weeping.

zh.name: 醋漬甜菜根
zh.summary: 市售罐裝的醋漬甜菜根，未開封放櫥櫃約可放 1 年。開封後要冷藏，可放 1～2 個月——醋能帶它走很遠，但開封後的罐子仍然是冷藏食品。
zh.pantry: 未開封的玻璃罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 1 年，若標示日期更早則以標示為準。讓甜菜根能常溫保存的是醃汁的酸度，加上加熱殺菌與密封；甜菜根本身是低酸性蔬菜，單靠它自己撐不到這裡。罐子要避免陽光直射，這麼紅的東西一曬就嚴重褪色；瓶蓋鼓起，或打開時噴汁的，請直接丟棄、不要試吃。
zh.fridge: 開封後冷藏，放 4 °C 以下 1～2 個月。請讓甜菜根保持浸在醃汁裡——露出液面的部分會變乾、變深色，也是最先長霉的地方——每次用乾淨的叉子，不要用手。至於自家醃、沒有經過常溫保存處理的甜菜根，從一開始就是冷藏品，不管食譜怎麼寫，都請這樣對待它。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給醋漬甜菜根的冷凍期限，而且冷凍本來就不划算。甜菜根大部分是裝在結實細胞裡的水，冷凍會把細胞脹破，解凍後又軟又出水、口感很差——醃漬保住的那份脆度，正是冷凍庫最會毀掉的東西。何況冷藏的期限已經夠寬裕了。
spoilage: 醃汁表面或瓶蓋內緣長霉。
醃汁變混濁、牽絲或變稠。
瓶蓋鼓起或滲漏，打開時有洩氣聲或噴汁。
甜菜根變軟爛，或聞起來有酵母、發酵味而不是乾淨的醋味。
tips: 讓甜菜根保持浸在醃汁裡；露出來的部分最先壞。
每次都用乾淨叉子，不要用手。
罐子避光存放——陽光褪色很快。
在蓋子上寫開封日期；一兩個月過得無聲無息。

faq.q: 醋漬甜菜根開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 浸在醃汁裡、放 4 °C 以下，1～2 個月。未開封放櫥櫃約 1 年。

faq.q: 醋漬甜菜根需要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 未開封不用。開封後要——標示上就寫著冷藏，而且封口一破，它就失去保護了。

faq.q: 醋漬甜菜根可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 沒有對應期限，也不值得——冷凍會脹破細胞，解凍後軟爛出水。
